column1: # Phase        | Color Band | Time       | What's Happening
# Drying       | Blue       | 0:00 – 4:00| Moisture leaves the bean. Temp recovers from the charge crash and climbs steadily.
# Maillard     | Yellow     | 4:00 – 8:00| Sugars and amino acids react. Color shifts tan → cinnamon. Berry aroma builds.
# First Crack  | Red        | 8:00 – 8:30| Audible popping begins at 360°F. Reduce flame to low.
# Development  | Green      | 8:30 – 9:00| Only 30–45 seconds. Drop at 372°F for maximum fruit.
# Key Visual Cues on the Curve:
# - The steep drop at 0:30 (325°F → 130°F) is the normal charge crash—your beans absorbing heat from the pan.
# - The curve steepens after 7:00 as the roast accelerates toward first crack. This is your warning to reduce flame.
# - The gentle rise from 360°F to 372°F is the development phase. Keep it short. Every extra 10°F past 372°F burns off more blueberry.
